controls.title: Controls
controls.description: Controls of ISO/IEC 27001, IEC 62443-2-1, NIS2 or your own catalogue, the Steward items mapped to them and the evidence they produced in a period.
controls.disclaimer: Steward collects evidence – it does not make you compliant. The catalogues contain the control identifiers and short topic names only; add the wording your organisation licensed by editing or importing a catalogue.
controls.noGapsText: Every control that is mapped to Steward items has evidence in the period.
controls.descriptionHelp: For example the wording your organisation licensed, or your own control description.
controls.noTags: No Steward item is mapped to this control yet.
controls.gapText: Gap: the mapped items produced no evidence in this period.
controls.noEvidence: No evidence – map processes, record types, monitors, report schedules or access reconciliation checks to this control.
controls.importHelp: JSON or YAML ({ key, name, version, description, controls: [{ ref, title, description }] }) or CSV with the columns ref, title, description. Existing controls get the new texts; nothing is removed.
controls.name: Name

accessChanges.title: Access changes
accessChanges.description: Every grant, revocation and change of access rights – documented by hand, created by runs, or documented after the access reconciliation found it.
accessChanges.subject: Subject
accessChanges.noMatch: No access change matches the filters.
accessChanges.emptyText: Document grants and revocations here – including changes made directly on a platform. Processes with a “Document access change” step create entries on their own.
accessChanges.tamperedHint: The content no longer matches the hash recorded when it was documented – it does not count as documentation. Check the audit log.
accessChanges.subjectIdHelp: User name, user id or technical user id on the platform
accessChanges.rightsHelp: Roles, groups or scopes – press Enter after each one
accessChanges.documentNowHelp: Freezes the entry (content hash). Leave it off to add attachments, e.g. screenshots or e-mails, before documenting.

reconciliation.title: Access reconciliation
reconciliation.description: Compares who actually has which access on a platform with the documented access changes. Changes without an entry show up here.
reconciliation.emptyText: A check takes a snapshot of the users and their roles and groups on a schedule and reports every change that has no access change entry.
reconciliation.noOpenText: Every change between the snapshots has an access change entry.
reconciliation.subject: Subject
reconciliation.snapshotsHelp: Snapshots are never changed. Each one is hash-chained to the previous one and recorded in the audit log.
reconciliation.importedHistory: Snapshots from before the move were verified against the imported audit history of the instance with key fingerprint {{fingerprint}} (moved here with a migration package).
reconciliation.documentHelp: Creates an access change entry marked “documented after the fact” and documents it right away. Attach evidence (e-mails, screenshots) later by starting a new revision of the entry.
reconciliation.dismissHelp: Only for changes that need no access change entry, e.g. a test account. The reason is recorded in the audit log. You cannot dismiss a change of your own access; with four-eyes dismissals (Settings), a second person confirms.
reconciliation.confirmDismissFor: Confirm the dismissal of the change of {{subject}}
reconciliation.confirmDismissTitle: Confirm the dismissal of the change of {{subject}}
reconciliation.ignoreRightsAdminOnly: Left out of the snapshots. Only administrators change them: grants of an ignored right are not reported.
reconciliation.name: Name
reconciliation.sourceHelp: Insights Hub: the identity management API of the platform. Dataset: a process that publishes the access snapshot shape (works for any platform).
reconciliation.datasetKeyHelp: Rows with subjectId, subjectName and right (one per assignment), e.g. ih.access-snapshot
reconciliation.scopeHelp: acme: members of the organisation or group with their role; acme/shop-web (GitLab: group/project): collaborators of the repository, outside collaborators marked
reconciliation.cronHelp: Five fields, at most every 15 minutes, e.g. 30 6 * * * (daily at 06:30)
reconciliation.notifyHelp: Besides the owner and the administrators
reconciliation.ignoreRightsHelp: Left out of the snapshots, e.g. a marker group of the access reviews that grants no access
reconciliation.noOpenAnywhere: None of your checks has open findings – every access change found is documented or dismissed.
reconciliation.snowflakeScopeHelp: Empty: every user with the roles granted to them. SHOP, SHOP.SALES or SHOP.SALES.ORDERS: every user who reaches objects there through their roles (and the roles granted to those), with the privilege. Technical users (type SERVICE) are marked.

packs.title: Evidence packs
packs.description: Signed ZIP exports for auditors: the evidence of some controls, a platform or a service in a period.
packs.limits: At most {{size}} per pack; packs are kept for {{days}} days.
packs.verifyText: Every file is listed with its SHA-256 in manifest.json, signed with the key of the audit checkpoints. Check it offline:
packs.emptyText: Choose controls (or a platform or service) and a period. Steward collects run protocols, records, access changes, reconciliation snapshots and findings, reports and an audit log excerpt.
packs.titlePlaceholder: e.g. ISO 27001 access control evidence Q4
packs.contentsHelp: The pack holds an index (PDF/A and index.json), run protocols, record PDFs with their files, access change entries, reconciliation snapshots and findings, scheduled reports and – for auditors and administrators – an audit log excerpt with a signed checkpoint.
packs.permissionsNote: The pack only holds what you may see. Creating and downloading it is recorded in the audit log.
